One key distinction between these methods is the difference between FTEs and on-board personnel. FTE employment is calculated based on the total number of hours worked and is equivalent to one year of full-time work (2,080 hours). On-board personnel, on the other hand, includes all employees, regardless of their work schedule.

OPM and OMB use different methods to measure the federal workforce, leading to different totals. For example, in FY2010, OPM reported 2.1 million on-board personnel, while OMB reported 1.9 million FTEs. This difference is due to the fact that FTEs do not represent individual employees but rather the amount of work being done.

The EHRI system is widely regarded as the most comprehensive resource on the size and scope of the federal workforce.

It offers five data cubes, including Employment, which provides quarterly data on the number of employees by agency and occupation, and Common Characteristics of Government, which provides an overview of OPM's federal employee databases.

The President's Budget, produced by OMB, also includes data on the federal workforce, but it uses the FTE method. This data is published annually and is used to manage employment levels in departments and agencies.
